title: Multiplicativity of the Tate Gauss norm
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. For $r\ge0$ let $T_r=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], so its coefficient families tend to zero in the cofinite filter. Equip it with $\|\sum_
u c_
u X^
u\|_G=\sup_
u|c_
u|$. For all $f,g\in T_r$, one has $\|fg\|_G=\|f\|_G\|g\|_G$. The multiplication is the Cauchy product. The case $r=0$, either zero factor, and trivial absolute values are included; completeness is not required.

proof.text:
Write $f=\sum c_
u X^
u$ and $g=\sum d_
u X^
u$. By [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], for every $\epsilon>0$ each coefficient family has only finitely many entries of absolute value at least $\epsilon$, and the product coefficient at $\gamma$ is $h_\gamma=\sum_{u+v=\gamma}c_ud_v$. This sum is finite: each coordinate of $u$ lies between $0$ and the corresponding coordinate of $\gamma$, and $v=\gamma-u$. If either series is zero then every product coefficient is zero and the required equality is $0=0$. Henceforth assume both series nonzero.

proof.text: For every $\gamma$, the finite set of decompositions $u+v=\gamma$ is nonempty (it contains $(0,\gamma)$). Multiplicativity of the absolute value gives $|c_ud_v|=|c_u||d_v|\le AB$. Apply the first clause of [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums] to the additive group of $K$ and $N=|\cdot|$; the strong triangle inequality and $|-x|=|x|$ hold for the stated absolute value. Hence $|h_\gamma|\le AB$. Taking the supremum proves $\|fg\|_G\le AB$ and also bounds that supremum without assuming completeness.

source.place: Bosch, Section 1.2, Gauss-norm discussion preceding Proposition 3, printed pp.8-9 (PDF pp.9-10); independent coefficient proof by Q31 replacing the residue-polynomial argument.

proof.text: Order $\mathbf N^r$ lexicographically, and take the largest indices $i,j$ in the finite attaining sets for $f,g$. Suppose $u+v=i+j$ and both $|c_u|=A$, $|d_v|=B$. Maximality gives $u\le i$ and $v\le j$ lexicographically. If $u<i$, at the first differing coordinate all earlier coordinates of $u,i$ agree and $u_k<i_k$; the sum equation gives all earlier coordinates of $v,j$ equal and $v_k>j_k$, contradicting $v\le j$. Thus $u=i$, and the sum equation forces $v=j$. Every other decomposition therefore has $|c_u|<A$ or $|d_v|<B$, and, since $A,B>0$, has $|c_ud_v|<AB=|c_id_j|$. For $r=0$ the index set has one empty tuple and there is no other decomposition.

source.place: Bosch, Section 1.2, Gauss-norm discussion preceding Proposition 3, printed pp.8-9 (PDF pp.9-10); independent coefficient proof by Q31 replacing the residue-polynomial argument.

proof.text: Apply the second clause of [lem-trf-nonarchimedean-finite-sums] to the finite Cauchy sum $h_{i+j}=\sum_{u+v=i+j}c_ud_v$, with distinguished pair $(i,j)$. Step 4 verifies every strict inequality required by that clause, and the absolute value verifies the same group hypotheses as in step 3. It follows that $|h_{i+j}|=|c_id_j|=AB$. Since a coefficient is bounded above by the supremum of all product coefficients, $AB\le\|fg\|_G$. Together with step 3 this is the asserted equality. Trivial absolute values cause no change: restricted families then have finite support, and the same maximal-index argument applies.
